text: Added to the knowledge base 2026-08-31 on request In one line: Proves checkpoint merging is algebraically equivalent to LR decay (merge weights invert to per-step gradient weights), so a constant LR plus a weighted merge of the last n checkpoints emulates cosine, linear, or 1-sqrt decay with no decay phase at all; beats a matched WSD anneal by ~1.3 points on a 16.3B MoE, with merge duration the dominant hyperparameter and EMA merging the worst. +1.28 points average of 41 base-model benchmarks, best WSM against best WSD checkpoint (62.67 to 63.95) +1.18 when both stop at WSD's 400B tokens (derived, Figure 3) · Table 1 0.25 points mean gap between a 4-checkpoint merge and a real 100B-token decay, at five points of a 10T run the cheap preview of a decayed model holds up (derived) · Figure 5(a) 28 of 41 benchmarks won by the best mean-merged checkpoint against the best WSD checkpoint 13 lost; the abstract's per-benchmark gains mix different checkpoints · Table 7 How far to trust it: Believe the algebra and the recipe: keep the learning rate flat, save checkpoints, average the last stretch, and you get about what a decay gives, plus a cheap preview of the decayed model.
